transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marcus Chen (Polaris), Aisha Rahman (Polaris), Daniel O'Neill (Polaris)

Automatic sections (auto-gen may be imperfect):
Topics: model catalog walkthrough, compatibility matrix, quantization tradeoffs, private deployment constraints, pilot scope

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick intros, then Priya will do a run through the model catalog and we'll talk benchmarks and which models we recommend for your short-conversational workload.
[00:23] Marcus (Polaris): Hi — Marcus here. We're most interested in consistent sub-120ms token latencies for default prompts, and we want cost to be reasonable. Also, we have on-prem GPU nodes for some sensitive data.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood SE): Great, thanks Marcus. I'll share my screen. I'm opening the Redwood Console catalog — just FYI names may look slightly different on the transcript, but the flow is: filters, benchmarks, compat matrix, then routing rules.
[01:10] Aisha (Polaris): Quick Q: when you say "benchmarks" are those your internal numbers or reproducible runs we can re-run?
[01:20] Priya: Good question. Benchmarks shown in catalog are standardized runs Redwood runs across hardware families; we attach raw logs and a reproducible benchmark harness you can run in your environment. There are per-model profiles: tail latency P50/P95, per-token cost estimation, and quantization friendliness flags.
[01:40] Daniel (Polaris): Are those measured with KV cache or without? Our workload benefits a lot from prefix caching.
[01:50] Priya: We include both. Catalog shows default numbers without KV cache and a "cached" column that reflects typical gains with prefix/K V cache. Note, caching benefits are workload-dependent.
[02:20] Jordan: We're going to focus on how you prioritize candidates: first, does model meet quality bar on your eval set; second, latency/cost targets; third, infra compatibility (quantization, GPU SM arch). We'll demo a filter-based shortlist.
[02:45] Priya: Okay, applying filters: conversation-friendly models, <150ms P95 on A10040GB equiv, 8-bit quantizable. That narrows to a handful — internally we call these the fast-low-cost cohort.
[03:10] Marcus: Can you call out the model names? We currently use a mixture of interna models and some open LLMs.
[03:20] Priya: Sure — on screen: Llama13b-v2-ish, Mistral-Instruct-7B variant, and a trimmed MPT-chat candidate. Names in the console match upstream repos; sometimes the transcript renames them slightly so I'll paste the exact model IDs after the call.
[03:48] Aisha: For private infra, what does Redwood Private look like? We need SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs to meet our compliance team.
[04:05] Jordan: Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem deployment. Integrations: SAML/SSO, SSO groups for RBAC, KMS/HSM support for key wrapping, and audit logging shipped to your SIEM. We also support VPC peering and private endpoints.
[04:35] Marcus: How about data residency? We sometimes need certain prompts to stay in-region.
[04:42] Jordan: You can pin regions per-route and we support routing policies that honor data residency tags. If you go fully private on-prem, data never leaves your network.
[05:00] Priya: Back to the catalog: you can expand a model and see compatibility matrix. Matrix rows: model variant, columns: hardware family (A100, H100, L40s, CPU-optim), quantization levels supported (fp16, int8, int4), latency estimates, and fallback suggestions.
[05:30] Daniel: Are the kernel selections automatic? Our infra team wants to know if we can pin kernels.
[05:40] Priya: Kernel selection is automatic by default — runtime will pick optimized kernels based on sequence length distribution. You can pin kernel families if you want deterministic behavior for debugging.
[06:00] Marcus: You mentioned fallback suggestions — what does that look like in practice?
[06:10] Priya: If an H100 model variant isn't available, routing can fall back to a quantized variant on A100 or to a slightly smaller model with a controlled delta in quality. The compatibility matrix encodes those compatible fallbacks for every variant.
[06:30] Aisha: Ok, let's talk about cost math. For short conv, tokens are mostly response tokens; do you show combined prompt+response cost predictions?
[06:45] Jordan: Yes — Console shows per-request token estimates and cost predictions, and Redwood Optimize can simulate batching/caching scenarios so you can see unit economics for different traffic mixes.
[07:05] Marcus: We also care about throughput — about 200 RPS at peak for a few minutes. How does dedicated vs hosted handle bursts?
[07:20] Priya: Dedicated capacity is for predictable throughput; you can configure burst pools and autoscale rules. Hosted API can handle bursts but subject to tiering and fair-share; for strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated or Private Dedicated capacity.
[07:40] Daniel: For our SREs, helpful to know: how do you instrument tracing? Does each token get a trace id?
[07:50] Priya: We emit trace ids and per-request spans; you can link to OpenTelemetry traces in your observability backend. There's also token-level latency breakdowns in the Console.
[08:20] Jordan: I'm going to switch to a quick benchmark demo using your short-chat prompt set (sample provided earlier). Priya, can you show 8-bit quantized run?
[08:35] Priya: Yep — running a local quick benchmarking harness in the Console lab. Heads-up: the demo uses a reproducible harness but the numbers on this call are illustrative.
[09:05] [screen noise, a short pause]
[09:20] Priya: Results up: Llama13b-v2-ish (fp16) P50 42ms P95 110ms; Llama13b-v2-ish (int8) P50 36ms P95 88ms; Mistral-7B-instr (int8) P50 30ms P95 75ms. So quantization shows significant tail-latency improvements for this prompt mix.
[09:50] Marcus: Those P95 numbers look good. Are they single-token or multi-token?
[09:55] Priya: These are end-to-end request latencies for typical ~24-token responses on our harness. Your distribution may vary — we recommended you run the harness with your real traffic.
[10:20] Aisha: Any gotchas with int8? We heard hallucination or quality regressions can happen.
[10:30] Priya: Absolutely — some models are more quant-friendly. Console flags models with higher quantization-induced regression risk. Also Redwood Optimize can run quality regression tests linked to your prompt sets and flag post-quantization failures.
[10:50] Daniel: If we need to do a canary, can Redwood do A/B model rollouts?
[10:58] Jordan: Yes — built-in rollouts: canary, weighted A/B, automatic rollback on quality or latency regression. You can set percent traffic and rule by user cohort or route.
[11:15] Marcus: About caching — in our flow tokens can be short but repeated; how does prefix caching work with privacy-sensitive data?
[11:30] Priya: Caching is optional and can be scoped per-route. For PII-sensitive prompts you can disable cache; for other routes you can enable prefix caching with TTL and encryption at rest.
[11:50] Marcus: And token-level encryption?
[11:55] Jordan: All persisted caches and logs can be encrypted with your KMS; in Private deployments keys stay in your HSM.
[12:10] Aisha: Performance of larger seq lengths — our long context only happens occasionally. Do you recommend mixing model families?
[12:25] Priya: Yes — routing policy can send long-context requests to a model variant and short ones to cheaper fast models. The catalog helps you map which variants are best for each context length.
[12:45] Marcus: Can we control routing by customer segment — e.g., premium users get low-latency model?
[12:55] Jordan: You can set routing rules by header, user attribute, or tenant tags. Premium routes can be pinned to dedicated capacity.
[13:20] Priya: Now I'm toggling to Optimize recommendations. For your traffic shape, Optimize suggests an 8-bit quantized Llama13b variant for most routes and an fp16 Mistral-7b fallback for edge cases. It also suggests a 2-second token generation cap to avoid runaway costs.
[13:50] Marcus: Nice. Curious how you simulate batching? Our traffic is spiky with microbursts.
[14:00] Priya: Optimize has a workload simulator — you provide arrival distribution and it estimates batching efficiency and token-level queueing delay. You can tune batch sizes and latency SLOs and it outputs cost tradeoffs.
[14:25] Daniel: On the security side, we need SOC2 and ISO-type artifacts — do you have pre-packaged evidence?
[14:35] Jordan: Yes — we have SOC2 Type II report, ISO attestation, and a security pack with encryption architecture and a pen-test summary. For Private we provide architecture diagrams and deployment runbooks.
[14:55] Aisha: What's typical timeline for a Private POC?
[15:00] Jordan: For a pilot usually 4–8 weeks. First week is environment prep and bench harness, weeks 2–4 are pilot runs/quality checks, week 5+ is tuning and ramp. Can be shorter for hosted pilots.
[15:20] Marcus: Cost question again — committed reserved vs on-demand dedicated. If we commit to a monthly capacity, what flexibility do we have?
[15:33] Jordan: Reserved capacity gives price breaks and guaranteed throughput; you can configure burst credits and we also have mid-contract scaling options. Pricing tiers and exact numbers I'll include in the follow-up.
[15:50] Priya: I want to highlight the compatibility matrix has a "risk" column — low/medium/high for things like quantization risk, kernel maturity on different cards, and memory fragmentation concerns. For example, the L40s shows medium risk for int4 on 13B variants; H100 had low risk.
[16:20] Marcus: We use a mix of H100s and older A100 nodes in different clusters. Will Redwood runtime route appropriately?
[16:30] Priya: Yes — smart routing can be policy based: prefer H100 first, fall back to A100, then to a smaller model if needed. You can also attach cost weights.
[16:50] Daniel: If we want to pin a model to an exact kernel for reproducibility, is that supported in Private?
[16:58] Priya: Yes — in Private you can pin kernels and runtime options; in hosted we provide pinned families for stable SLOs.
[17:15] Marcus: Let's talk about observability — we need per-tenant cost breakouts and token-level chargeback.
[17:25] Jordan: Console has per-tenant dashboards, token-level breakdown, and you can export raw usage to your billing system. We also support webhooks for anomaly alerts.
[17:45] Aisha: Any limitations on model licensing or redistributing open weights?
[17:55] Jordan: We respect upstream licenses and surface license type in the catalog. For Private you manage weights in your environment; we provide legal guidance but not legal advice.
[18:10] Priya: Jumping ahead — running a short canned benchmark of Mistral-7b-instr quantized on your prompt set now in the private sandbox we spun up.
[18:30] [typing, short pause]
[18:45] Priya: Mistral int8 P50 28ms P95 70ms; corpus quality score on your eval harness is 0.84 (baseline 0.86 on fp16). That 0.02 delta might be acceptable depending on your tolerance. Optimize can give a per-prompt delta distribution.
[19:10] Marcus: A small drop might be okay for most customers, but for compliance/legal prompts we need fp16. Can we route sensitive prompts to non-quantized variant?
[19:20] Jordan: Absolutely — you can tag routes and set quantization policies per-route.
[19:35] Daniel: We need to test memory exhaustion scenarios — will your runtime give graceful degradation?
[19:45] Priya: Runtime includes graceful fallback rules and can trigger a lighter model or a rate-limit if memory pressure is detected. We also keep circuit breaker metrics visible in Console.
[20:05] Marcus: Do you provide an SDK? Our stack is Python + Go.
[20:12] Jordan: Yes — Python/Go/Node SDKs with examples for streaming, function/tool calls, and structured outputs.
[20:25] Aisha: One more: for our legal team — we want deterministic logging retention policies and ability to purge conversation history on request. Is that supported?
[20:36] Jordan: Data retention policies are configurable; purge APIs are available and on Private deployments you control retention entirely.
[20:50] Priya: We're about halfway in, so quick recap: we showed how to filter the catalog for latency/cost/quantization-friendly models, looked at compatibility matrices, ran short quantized benchmarks, and discussed routing, security, and pilot timelines.
[21:10] Marcus: Sounds useful. For the pilot, we'll provide two real prompt sets: short support chat and a longer context analytic summary. We'll want detailed quality metrics for both.
[21:25] Jordan: Great — action items captured. Priya, any caveats to note before we wrap?
[21:33] Priya: Caveat — quantization and kernel maturity vary across upstream model forks, so for PR-sensitive production you should run Redwood Optimize's regression tests and canary before full rollout. Also, some model names in the catalog map to community names — we'll send exact model IDs to avoid confusion.
[21:55] Aisha: Can you also share a sample benchmark harness and the instructions to run it in our GCP project?
[22:02] Jordan: Yes — I'll include a step-by-step runbook and a public repo link.
[22:20] Marcus: Timeline constraint — legal needs to review security pack; can you give us materials within a week?
[22:28] Jordan: We'll aim to share SOC2 pack and compatibility matrix by Monday (2025-11-24).
[22:40] [brief cross-talk]
[22:50] Priya: Quick question from my side — Marcus, can you confirm whether the on-prem cluster has mixed PCIe/HBM nodes? That affects kernel selection.
[22:59] Marcus: Yes, mixed HBM (H100) and PCIe (A100) — we'll share instance types.
[23:10] Daniel: If we hit a quality regression post-quantization, is there a support SLA for rollbacks?
[23:20] Jordan: Enterprise customers get priority incident support and we can configure automatic rollback policies. We'll include SLO language in the follow-up.
[23:35] Aisha: Any notes on egress cost if we use hosted API for some traffic and private for others?
[23:45] Priya: Console includes estimated egress costs per-region; we can model hybrid cost scenarios in Optimize.
[24:00] Jordan: I'm going to read back the next steps: Jordan will send compatibility matrix, pricing tiers, SOC2 pack; Priya will run quantized latency test on Polaris prompt set and share logs; Marcus will provide prompt sets and infra instance details. We'll schedule a pilot kick-off — suggested window next week.
[24:30] Marcus: That works. Thanks everyone.
[24:35] [wrapping up comments, people leaving the call over next few minutes]
[25:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email.
